title: decision-transition-basis-misattributed

proposition.statement: A relying system must not represent a material decision transition as an authority change when the causal basis was instead a change in evidence, policy, lifecycle state, correction, or evaluation context.

preconditions: A material decision changes from a prior outcome to a different outcome.
The change can be caused by one or more distinguishable inputs such as authority, evidence, policy, lifecycle state, correction, or evaluation context.
The actual causal basis is not an authority grant, transfer, or revocation.

trigger.statement: The system records, communicates, or relies on the changed decision as though authority changed merely because the outcome became more or less permissive.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence linking the prior and current decision to the material inputs evaluated for each.
Evidence establishing whether authority actually changed across the decision transition.
Evidence of the governing policy and whether policy applicability or version changed.
Evidence of any lifecycle-state change material to the transition.
Evidence identifying the causal transition category and any correction or evaluation-context change.

falsification.condition: A decision record asserts an authority change while the only evidenced material change is evidence, policy, lifecycle state, correction, or evaluation context.
A more permissive outcome is treated as proof that new authority was granted when no authority event can be established.
The system cannot reconstruct why the outcome changed but reports the transition as verified authority change.
